problem: IL pipelines (BC, DAgger) for VLN-CE suffer from distribution shift and ambiguous expert actions after deviation. Closed-loop RL on micro actions is sample-inefficient because of hundreds-step horizons and sparse reward, so prior RL work falls back on open-loop RFT or distance-based dense rewards.
motivation: RL learns directly from task outcomes and is a natural fit for closed-loop navigation, but only if the decision horizon is short enough for credit assignment. Topological graphs with frontier selection shrink the horizon from hundreds of micro steps to 5-20 macro decisions, so closed-loop RL with a sparse outcome reward becomes tractable.
key_idea: Reformulate VLN-CE as a hierarchical MDP and run closed-loop PPO on the macro frontier-selection MDP of a topological graph, using a training-free low-level controller as the state transition and an action-aware value head that sees the dynamic frontier set.
insight: The macro action space is what makes closed-loop RL work: with an identical backbone, micro-action closed-loop RFT gains only +0.6 SR after about 120 h (with high reward variance), while macro PPO gains +3.0 SR in about 16 h. The action-aware critic matters: a history-only critic drops the gain to +1.1 SR and needs about 25 h. RFT gain stays roughly constant (+6.2 to +7.0 in SR+SPL) across 25-100% pretraining data, so it is orthogonal to data scaling. A sparse outcome reward (Success+SPL+nDTW) beats dense geodesic-distance reward, which encourages geometric shortcuts over instruction fidelity.
method: Hierarchical MDP: macro MDP over topological graph frontier nodes (plus STOP), with a micro MDP handled by a deterministic rotate-then-forward-with-tryout controller as the transition

Topological graph and encoding: waypoint predictor generates frontiers; each explored node stores 12 RGB-D views compressed to 4 directional tokens by attention pooling; frontier tokens inherit angular-grid features; step and pose embeddings

Graph-aware cross-modal fusion: cross- and self-attention layers with GASA (spatial bias from path distance and sin/cos orientation via MLP), plus a text-guided graph branch concatenated to the output
Action-aware value head: state expanded to the full graph including unvisited frontiers; a learnable query attention-pools G_out into a scalar V, sharing the backbone with the actor

Graph-based PPO with outcome reward: terminal reward R_T = Success + SPL + nDTW, GAE, KL regularisation to the DAgger reference, strictly on-policy (1 epoch, 256 trajectories per update, 500 iterations)
Three-stage training: pretraining (Prevalent, LVLM-reannotated Prevalent, RxR-Marky, R2R, RxR), DAgger with value-head warm-up, then closed-loop RFT

setting.backbone: Graph Transformer planner (CLIP ViT-B/32 RGB encoder frozen, DD-PPO ResNet-50 depth encoder frozen, RoBERTa text encoder, 2-layer panorama encoder, 4-layer cross-modal fusion, d=768), trained from pretraining, DAgger and PPO
setting.training_data: Pretraining on Prevalent, Prevalent_LVLM_Aug (LVLM-re-annotated instructions), RxR-Marky, R2R train and RxR train; DAgger and RFT separately on R2R-CE and RxR-CE
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 views) with odometry, topological graph memory
setting.action_space: macro: select a frontier node (or STOP) from the topological graph; low-level rotate-then-forward heuristic controller executes it
setting.privileged: none (waypoint predictor and odometry used; no GT map)

results: Ours-RFT reaches 68.1 SR / 57.3 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 62.3 SR / 66.8 nDTW on RxR-CE val-unseen with only 0.5B parameters, beating HNR (61.0 SR on R2R-CE) and 7B StreamVLN (56.9 SR). RFT adds +3.0 SR and +3.8 SPL over the DAgger initialization on R2R-CE, and PPO beats GRPO (+1.7) and SAC (+2.1).
limitations: Relies on a waypoint predictor, restricting the macro action space to its outputs with no global reachability guarantee
Heuristic low-level controller; only evaluated in simulation, sim-to-real gap not addressed
Ablations are only on R2R-CE val-unseen; orthogonality claim rests on a single figure with four data scales
